external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that initiates communication with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application serves browser requests and puts jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs, does the work, and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding jobs placed by the web application for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: A database read and written by the background worker and containing the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the web application reads its settings, including queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the worker reads its settings, including database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to application
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: read and write records
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database, including application log records.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: … the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The network zone outside the system's network where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The system's web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker, database, and config stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is reachable from the public internet.
assumptions.basis: A user's browser talks to it across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work, rather than as a web-facing application.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The config store holds the credentials the web application needs.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The config store holds the credentials the worker needs.
